content.text: characterized by macules or small papules after initiation of drug TX
▪︎MC occurs 5-14d after the initiation of the offending
drug or within 1-2d in previously sensitized individuals
▪︎for short courses (e.g., antibiotics), eruption may appear
Self-limited, localized SQ (or submucosal) swelling resulting from extravasation of fluid into interstitium affecting mucosal tissues of face, lips, tongue, larynx, hands, feet, & genitalia
▪︎spontaneous resolution in hours to a few days
accompanied by other allergic reaction SXS
(urticaria, flushing, pruritis, bronchospasm, stridor, throat tightness, hypotension)
Bradykinin-mediated (ACEI-induced or hereditary d/t C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency): angioedema
If there is no information to suggest an external cause & the patient has isolated angioedema (w/o pruritis or urticaria), then C4 levels & a C1 inhibitor antigenic level should be obtained
Edema of superficial skin layers d/t histamine-related ⇡ vascular permeability
: release of vasodilators (histamine, bradykinin, kallikrein, PGs) from mast cells & basophils
: foods, meds, heat or cold, stress, insect bites, environmental, & infection
circumscribed hives or wheals (blanchable, raised, erythematous areas on the skin or mucous membranes)
